source_ref: OSF osf.io/ad6b3 (component z2mgv: ex.dataset.csv, pa.dataset.csv, code_book_BFI_N.txt, retest.data.oasis.odsis.sav, data.pa.aft.imp.Rds; component cjw3q: CZ_short_OASIS_ODSIS.Rmd = osf.io/k5bvs, lines 218-232 and 284-298); data/CV_OASIS_ODSIS_PPE_Novak_2020.R; Sandora et al. 2021, Int J Environ Res Public Health 18:10337, doi:10.3390/ijerph181910337, Section 2.2.4 (CC BY 4.0); RSES wording per Rosenberg 1965, in the Morris Rosenberg Foundation / University of Maryland circulated form
note: Code IS the source column name: data/CV_OASIS_ODSIS_PPE_Novak_2020.R does select(starts_with('RSES')) + pivot_longer on ex.dataset.csv / pa.dataset.csv, so there is no positional or rename step -- but those columns carry no text at any level (plain semicolon-delimited CSVs, no variable labels, no RSES codebook in the deposit), so mapping_basis is reconstructed, not data_labels. The ten columns are reconstructed as the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale in the widely circulated Morris Rosenberg Foundation / UMD item order, on the ground that that version is reverse-keyed at positions 2, 5, 6, 8, 9 and nowhere else, and the study's own analysis script (osf.io/k5bvs, CZ_short_OASIS_ODSIS.Rmd lines 220-224 / 286-290) independently reverses exactly RSES_2, RSES_5, RSES_6, RSES_8, RSES_9 -- 1 of C(10,5)=252 possible 5-subsets -- and the live data reproduces that polarity split (see verify script). Note this is NOT Rosenberg's 1965 numbering, whose reverse items are 3, 5, 8, 9, 10. Response direction is fixed by the .Rmd's two-step recode (reverse {2,5,6,8,9}, then reverse all ten 'to indicate that higher RSES score refers to higher self-esteem'), which is only self-consistent if the raw coding runs 1 = strongly agree ... 4 = strongly disagree with {1,3,4,7,10} positively worded; corroborated by the deposit's scored frame data.pa.aft.imp.Rds (means 5-raw for {1,3,4,7,10}, raw for {2,5,6,8,9}) and by the paper's stated 0-30 total range. The table stores RAW responses, so anchors are shipped in one direction for all ten items. Wording is the canonical English RSES text, because the administration was Czech and no Czech wording is recoverable from the deposit or the paper; anchors 'Strongly agree'/'Agree'/'Disagree'/'Strongly disagree' are the canonical four. Instructions are the first sentence of the canonical instruction block only; the circle-SA/A/D/SD remainder was dropped as it describes a paper form and this study ran online. Rights: the source IRW copied from is the CC BY 4.0 MDPI paper and its CC-BY OSF deposit, and no non-commercial or no-redistribution sentence could be quoted for the RSES itself, so wording_rights is omitted.
public_note: Item text for this Czech-administered Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale table is the canonical English RSES wording, not the Czech wording respondents actually read -- the OSF deposit and the paper publish neither the Czech items nor any per-item labels. The item codes are reconstructed as the widely circulated RSES ordering (reverse-keyed at 2, 5, 6, 8, 9), not Rosenberg's 1965 ordering, on the basis of the study's own scoring script; that pins each item's polarity class, the response direction and RSES_8, but does not distinguish RSES_3 from RSES_4, RSES_1 from RSES_10, or the four remaining reverse-keyed items from one another. Responses are stored raw, with 1 = 'Strongly agree' and 4 = 'Strongly disagree' for every item including the reverse-worded ones.

The Japanese Journal of Personality 24(1):26-37, https://doi.org/10.2132/personality.24.26 -- Appendix 2 (item list) and Figure 1B / footnote 2 (item-number correspondence). note: IRW item codes are the S1 CSV column names carried through unchanged by data/daiku_2021_prolific_liars.py (a melt, no rename), so they name the subscale and a within-subscale index but no wording. Within-subscale order: DTDD-J presents Machiavellianism as its items 1/4/7/10, Psychopathy as 2/5/8/11, Narcissism as 3/6/9/12 (Figure 1B), and Tamura's footnote 2 maps those to Jonason & Webster's original 1-4/5-8/9-12 in the same relative order, so index i is the i-th item of the subscale under either numbering convention. That is an order inference, not a labelled tie -- hence paper_order, and status PARTIAL in verification. item_text_translated is Jonason & Webster's (2010) original English for the correspondingly numbered items; the English for instructions and for the two scale anchors was produced by IRW (no published English exists for the DTDD-J's own instruction/anchor wording). Anchors 1 = 全くあてはまらない and 5 = 非常にあてはまる are the only labelled points in Appendix 2; 2-4 are left blank rather than padded. Rights: no non-commercial or no-redistribution clause is stated on the J-STAGE record (Journal Free) or in the PDF, so the Step-0 rights rule does not fire; the response data's own source is CC BY 4.0.
public_note: The DTDD-J was administered in Japanese; item_text_translated reproduces Jonason and Webster's (2010) original English for the correspondingly numbered items, but the English shown for the instructions and for the two scale anchors was translated by IRW rather than by the study's authors.

source_ref: Dalky et al. 2020 PeerJ 8:e9990 doi:10.7717/peerj.9990 (CC BY 4.0), supplementary peerj-08-9990-s001.sav via Europe PMC PMC7519719 supplementaryFiles; data/dalky_2020_sf36.py; block stems from RAND 36-Item Health Survey 1.0 (public domain, RAND Corporation)
note: SF-36 block of the PeerJ CC BY 4.0 supplementary .sav (peerj-08-9990-s001.sav, Europe PMC PMC7519719). mapping_basis=data_labels: every one of the 35 columns carries an SPSS variable label giving its item and a value-label set giving its options, and data/dalky_2020_sf36.py melts those columns by name (the IRW item code IS the source column name, typo 'physcial2' included), so there is no positional or renaming step to get wrong. Labels were cleaned deliberately: the trailing ' : CATEGORICAL Question' / ' :' suffixes and the surrounding single quotes on physical1/physcial2/physical5 were stripped; nothing else (casing, spelling, punctuation) was altered. LANGUAGE: the paper's Instruments section states the Arabic version of the SF-36 was administered, and the .sav contains zero Arabic characters across all 190 variable labels and every value label, so the administered wording is not recoverable from the deposit. The English in the base fields is the study's own rendering in those labels (note 'Okay'/'Bad' rather than the canonical 'Fair'/'Poor'), the _translated columns are empty, and text_source=translated_substitute records the fallback. SECTION PROMPTS: the .sav has no block-header variables, so the five block stems are the canonical public-domain RAND 36-Item Health Survey 1.0 English wording, supplied because 20 of the 35 item labels are sentence fragments that carry no referent without them and because L8_1/L8_2 and L9_1/L9_2 have identical labels that only the block stem distinguishes. Block identity is not assumed: L8 has 4 items and L9 has 3, exactly the SF-36's role-physical/role-emotional split in questionnaire order, and in the raw .sav the L8 block mean correlates 0.511 with the 9-item physical-functioning mean vs 0.413 for L9, while L9 correlates 0.223 with the 5-item mental-health mean vs 0.165 for L8. The six standalone items (H1hlthgeneral, H2healthcomplastyr, L10, L14, pain4wks, paineffect) are complete questions in their own labels and sit in a blank-prompt section _1; instructions left blank because neither the .sav nor the paper publishes any. Step 3b: the live set is the SF-36 minus one physical-functioning item (9 of 10) and minus one general-health-perception item (4 of 5) -- 35 rather than 36 -- which the processing script already documents; per-item response ranges match the instrument's mixed formats exactly (5/5 general and transition, 3 for the 9 PF items, 2 for L8/L9, 5 for L10/L14/paineffect/L15, 6 for pain4wks and the 9 L13 items). RIGHTS: the wording shipped was copied from the CC BY 4.0 PeerJ deposit's own SPSS labels, which under the ECR-R ruling is the licence that governs; the SF-36 trademark holder (Optum/QualityMetric) licenses the instrument commercially rather than stating a non-commercial clause, and no non-commercial or no-redistribution sentence could be quoted, so wording_rights is omitted. The block stems are RAND's public-domain RAND-36 1.0. Precedent: bukurov_2022_sf36 shipped on the same basis in batch_009.
public_note: This SF-36 was administered in Arabic; the item and option wording shipped here is the study's own English rendering, taken from its SPSS variable and value labels, not the Arabic wording respondents read (the deposit publishes no Arabic text). The five block stems are the canonical public-domain RAND-36 English wording, supplied because the data file carries no block headers and many item labels are fragments without them. The table holds 35 of the SF-36's 36 items -- one physical-functioning item and one general-health-perception item are absent from the source file.

note: item_text is the source workbook's own column headers, verbatim, in column order; data/dasilva_2019_hexaco24.py names column n HEXACO24_n, so the code IS the header position and no wording was inferred. source_ref: CRAN diffIRT 1.5, man/rotation.Rd (title 'Responses and Response Times to 10 Mental Rotation Items'; \format block lists the rotation angle of items 1-10) and data/rotation.rda; IRW script data/diffIRT_dat.R; dictionary URL https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/diffIRT/index.html; package licence GPL-2, no NC or no-redistribution clause
note: IRW item code i comes from data/diffIRT_dat.R's item <- 1:ncol(rt) over rotation[,1:10]/[,11:20], i.e. source columns X[i]/T[i]; the Rd numbers its angle list over the same 1-10.
